title: Uber's Secure AI Framework Governs Autonomous AI Agents Across Their Lifecycle
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/uber-secure-ai-framework/en/headerimage/uber-open-search-semantic-1794769460527.jpeg"/><p>In a recent article, Uber Engineering highlights the limitations of traditional identity and API controls in securing AI agents that dynamically reason over external content and take real-world actions. Uber developed a framework to determine whether an agent's action is appropriate given the user's request, the agent's intended purpose, its permissions, and the context of the interaction.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Anthropic Outlines Its AI-Powered Code Review Process for Claude Code
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/claude-code-review/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794735663601.jpg"/><p>Anthropic has outlined how the Claude Code team handles code reviews as AI agents increasingly contribute to its codebase. The approach relies on multiple layers of automated verification, AI-powered reviews, and risk-based human approval, aiming to reduce manual review time without increasing regressions or production incidents.</p> <i>By Robert Krzaczyński</i>

title: Cloudflare Introduces Private Origins for Application Services
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cloudflare-private-origins/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793395278236.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare recently made Application Services for Private Origins generally available, allowing public traffic to reach applications hosted on private networks without exposing their IP addresses or opening inbound firewall ports. Private-to-private connectivity is not yet supported.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Cohere Finding Shows Self-Hosted Open-Weight Models Still Need Egress Controls
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/cohere-open-weight-egress-risk/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794703595152.jpg"/><p>Cohere recently reported that one of Alibaba’s newest Qwen3.8 models attempted to upload a probe file to a storage container in Beijing while explicitly stating in its reasoning trace that no tools would be triggered. While there is no evidence of intentional backdooring, the report is a reminder that, even for self-hosted agents based on open-weight models, egress risks exist and need mitigation.</p> <i>By Bruno Couriol</i>

title: Node.js Brings Debounce, Throttle, and PKCS#12 Parsing Into Core Modules
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/nodejs-debounce-throttle/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794593143949.jpg"/><p>Node.js 26.10.0 adds util.debounce() and util.throttle(), plus util.markPromiseAsHandled(), to the core library. It also introduces crypto.parsePKCS12() for reading .p12 and .pfx bundles, and extends the experimental Virtual File System to node:ffi. The additions reduce the need for some userland dependencies. Node.js 26 is now Active LTS.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Google Cloud Moves the Compute Engine API to Immutable Date-Based Versions
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/compute-engine-api-versioning/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794296072866.jpg"/><p>Google Cloud has made date-based versioning of the Compute Engine API generally available, replacing the single mutable /v1 surface with immutable quarterly snapshots such as 2026-09-01, selected per request with a header or query parameter. New versions can change defaults, error formats, and IAM checks without touching /v1 callers, a model Azure Resource Manager and Stripe have used for years.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Open Source DocumentDB 1.0 Reaches General Availability
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>DocumentDB 1.0 is the first generally available release of the open source, MIT-licensed document database built on PostgreSQL, with compatibility for the MongoDB wire protocol. Most MongoDB drivers, tools, and queries work without changes.</p> <i>By Renato Losio</i>

title: Siri AI Developer Preview Lets iOS, iPadOS, and macOS Apps Integrate with Siri
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/apple-siri-ai-integration/en/headerimage/ios-27-virtualization-1794583601204.jpeg"/><p>Apple released the Siri AI Developer Preview in the 27.3 beta releases of its operating systems, enabling developers and apps to integrate with the assistant and hand off actions to it. During the Preview, access to Siri AI is restricted to developer builds and internal TestFlight testers.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Google Open Sources Ambient Quality Agent (AQuA) to Diagnose Production AI Agent Failures
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/google-ambient-agent-prod/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1792894383462.jpg"/><p>Google has open-sourced AQuA, a reference implementation that analyzes production AI agent sessions, verifies recurring failure patterns, and investigates root causes against deployed source snapshots. In a 32-session replay, developers reduced seat selection bypasses from 15 sessions to two and dietary preference omissions from seven to zero after prompt changes.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Netflix Turns Operational Data Into a Knowledge Graph for AI-Driven Observability
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/netflix-ai-driven-observability/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1793693699423.jpg"/><p>Netflix is developing an ontology-driven knowledge graph to accelerate production investigations and provide AI agents with a shared understanding of its operational environment.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: The Influence Toolkit
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/bbc-software-architecture-influence/en/mediumimage/henry-wilson-medium-1792653480613.jpg"/><p>Henry Wilson shares actionable tools from the BBC Sounds re-architecture to help senior engineering leaders drive technical strategy. He discusses building buy-in, navigating active resistors, using RFCs and ADRs, and balancing tradeoffs - showing that effective software architecture is fundamentally about communication, relationship-building, and organizational influence.</p> <i>By Henry Wilson</i>

title: Podcast: Doing The Right Thing: Accountability In The Age Of AI Coding Summary
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/accountability-age-ai-coding-summary/en/smallimage/engineering-culture-500-1794303925695.jpg"/><p>In this podcast, Shane Hastie, Lead Editor for Culture & Methods, spoke to Hugo Venturini about who is accountable when AI writes the code, how AI is reshaping code review and traditional engineering roles, and how leaders build a culture of transparency and psychological safety.</p> <i>By Hugo Venturini</i>

title: Dropbox Shares How Its In-House Cookie Auditor Tests Consent Behaviour Across 200+ Web Surfaces
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/dropbox-cookie-auditor/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1794331089979.jpg"/><p>Dropbox engineers described a Playwright-based auditor that checks cookie consent behavior across more than 200 web surfaces. It runs three tests per page: US visitor, EU visitor, and Global Privacy Control signal. Cookie rules are kept outside the code. A companion tool finds live URLs. Weekly reports separate likely violations from false positives.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: Technical Debt is Social; it is the Price of Learning by Doing
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/11/tech-debt-learning-doing/en/headerimage/header-1794404225270.jpg"/><p>Technical debt is not necessarily a sign of poor engineering. It can be the price of learning through software in use. As AI accelerates code production beyond our capacity to understand code and context, technical debt increasingly becomes a sociotechnical challenge.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: Presentation: Opening the Black Box: Critical Explainability for AI Agent Tool Selection with Kiji Inspector
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/explainable-ai-llm-agent-decisions/en/mediumimage/HannesHapke-medium-1793278895069.jpeg"/><p>Hannes Hapke shares how Dataiku’s open-source Kiji Inspector applies Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) directly to decision tokens to expose why agents pick specific tools. Moving past superficial chain-of-thought narratives, he discusses causal ablation, layer activation extraction via patched vLLM engines, and production monitoring workflows for software architects and senior engineering leaders.</p> <i>By Hannes Hapke</i>
